paragraphs.text: Active exploitation of Cisco BroadWorks and OpenWave flaws despite available patches, combined with the discovery of 33 critical vulnerabilities forcing the N-able N-central platform offline, demonstrates that vulnerability management controls are not keeping pace with exploited flaws in widely deployed infrastructure. The revocation of eMudhra intermediate CA certificates due to private key mishandling during certificate generation further weakens trust in PKI-based authentication controls. Vulnerability and asset owners should confirm affected product deployments and verify remediation status, while identity and access owners must assess trust store impacts from revoked certificates.

Third-party breaches at Baker Tilly, Notion's AI provider Fireworks AI, and Maersk's acquired legacy system reveal that data protection and supplier assurance controls do not consistently extend to supply chain dependencies and inherited assets. These incidents exposed personal information, AI chat transcripts, and extracted data through compromised third-party providers and unmanaged legacy platforms. Supplier risk owners should review affected supplier dependencies and assurance evidence, while data and privacy owners must assess sensitive data access restrictions across AI supply chains and acquired systems.
